subject: Standardized Info Request — prompt/log retention windows and training opt-out
messages:
From: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@cardiotech.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: security@cardiotech.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: details on prompt/log retention and training opt-out

Hi Olga,

Thanks for agreeing to take our SIG follow-up calls. We got the initial SIG matrix back and have a couple of targeted clarification items from our security and privacy teams before we close the loop on vendor assessment:

1) Please confirm the default retention windows for prompt input logs, model outputs, and KV/prefix caches across Redwood Hosted and Dedicated deployments.
2) For customer data that may be PII or PHI, what is the process and timeline to classify and purge logs upon request (i.e., customer deletion/opt-out)?
3) Does Redwood ever use customer prompt/response data to train generalized model weights? If so, how is that opt-out enforced and audited?
4) If a customer requests training opt-out for a particular dataset or workspace, what artifacts do you provide as evidence?

Could you provide short answers and any supporting artifacts we can attach to our vendor assessment? We need a timeline by EOD tomorrow if possible.

Appreciate it —
Priya
Priya Sharma
Senior InfoSec Analyst, CardioTech
priya.sharma@cardiotech.com

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@cardiotech.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: details on prompt/log retention and training opt-out

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers and I attached an evidence pack (diagram + retention matrix). If you need any of this inserted into the SIG spreadsheet cells, let me know and I can paste.

1) Default retention windows (Hosted / Dedicated):
   - Prompt input logs: Hosted — 30 days (default, configurable down to 0 for ephemeral mode). Dedicated — customer-configurable; default 90 days for audit retention unless customer requests shorter.
   - Model outputs (generation responses): Hosted — 30 days; Dedicated — configured with workspace retention rules (default 90 days).
   - KV/prefix caches: Ephemeral in-memory by default; persisted caches (for Dedicated) retained per customer policy — typically 7 days snapshot for performance telemetry, can be set to 0.

2) Customer-requested purge / classification workflow:
   - Submit a data subject or workspace deletion request via our Console API or Support ticket (link in attachment).
   - We run an automated scan to identify matching artefacts across logs, prefixes, and stored artifacts; manual review only for disputed cases.
   - Typical SLA: Hosted — bulk purge completed within 5 business days from request (audit trail generated). Dedicated — purge completed within 3 business days when Redwood has admin access; if customer self-hosts persistence, we provide an ops playbook and verification steps.

3) Use of customer data for training:
   - Redwood does not use customer-owned production data to train public or shared model weights by default. Hosted customers may opt-in to aggregated telemetry programs; that is explicitly consent-based and surfaced during onboarding.
   - For customers that opt-out (default for enterprise/Dedicated tiers), we exclude their workspace identifiers from all training pipelines. Training data pipelines ingest datasets from opt-in buckets only.
   - Auditing: We maintain pipeline manifests and dataset provenance logs (SHA’ed manifests). We can export a manifest showing that your workspace or workspace-id was excluded during a given training run window.

4) Evidence and artifacts provided for opt-out:
   - Signed DPA addendum confirming training opt-out (we can attach a template — attached dpa_addendum_v1.docx).
   - Exportable exclusion manifest (CSV) and pipeline provenance (retention_matrix + run manifests).
   - Audit log entries showing the exclusion operation and the support ticket/DPA sign-off.

Attachments included: redwood_SIG_data_flow_diagram.pdf (architecture + dataflow), redwood_prompt_retention_matrix.csv (detailed windows & config knobs), dpa_addendum_v1.docx (template).

If you want, Marissa (cc’d) and I can hop on a short call to walk through the audit artifacts.

Cheers,
Olga Petrov
Security Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Olga —

Thanks, this is very helpful. A couple of quick clarifications from Privacy:

- For Hosted customers, when you say "configurable down to 0 for ephemeral mode", can you confirm whether 0 means "never written to disk" or "written briefly and then deleted within the window"? We need assurance that ephemeral = no persistent copy in S3 or similar.
- For the exclusion manifest: can you provide a sample export that shows a workspace-level exclusion entry and the SHA/provenance fields you mentioned? A redacted sample is fine.

We'd like to include those two items in our vendor package. If you can drop them by EOD that helps our procurement review.

Regards,
Priya

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@cardiotech.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: details on prompt/log retention and training opt-out

Priya — quick follow-ups inline and attachments updated.

- Ephemeral semantics: Ephemeral = not persisted to durable object storage by default. For Hosted ephemeral mode we route to in-memory KV and scrub any transient write-back hooks; there are no durable S3 objects created. Our retention_matrix row now shows explicit flags (persisted: false) for ephemeral mode.

- Sample exclusion manifest: Attached a redacted_csv_exclusion_manifest.csv (in the evidence pack URL) showing workspace_id, excluded_flag, exclusion_reason, manifest_sha256, pipeline_run_id, and timestamp. The manifest SHA is computed over the manifest payload and signed by our ingestion service.

Next steps: if CardioTech wants a signed DPA addendum, sign the attached doc and return via DocuSign (link above) and Marissa will coordinate the verification export and one-time audit proof (pipeline manifest) in the week following signature.

Let us know if you'd like a 30-minute verification call — we can set it up today.

Best,
Olga
